exclude: Playfield matrix buffers. The viewport draw at $185D, $1897 and $18BD generates 800 character cells in the first buffer, and the loop at $1916 mirrors its four pages to the second. The remaining cells lie past the displayed playfield rows. The sprite writer uses the final eight addresses of both matrices as pointer registers.

Resident release code from the language load. Bytes are identical at the language and quest hand-overs and the quest load write map records no stores in this interval. The entry reads the resident byte at $C980.
Processor port and zero-page workspace. $3B3D clears bytes $02–$FF and the game fills individual pointers, control masks and counters as it runs.
Installed software interrupt and KERNAL vectors. The quest IRQ setup patches $0316 and $0317 during initialization.
Object-construction scratch filled by the map action and deferred spawn paths before they call $1940.
Intermediate object piece positions, sprite bytes and count generated by $1DA6 and filtered by $1E61.
The per-frame sprite list arrays. $2127 fills them from object, item and projectile state before raster display.
New viewport character edge buffers produced by the renderers and copied into the next matrix by the scroll routines.
Generated viewport edge colours. The edge builders translate the character bytes through the world colour table before these values are copied to colour RAM.
Generated hardware sprite pointers for the spell HUD. The setup and selection routines write these pointer bytes from the active spell indices.
Generated 256-byte unpacked map action row. $37AD fills it from the stored compressed row. The spell display also fills its first 64 bytes with $AA.
Six object slots represented as separate per-field arrays. The constructor at $1940 fills the active slot, and the following object-motion code updates those fields.

comments.text: Requested paired sound effect. A negative value leaves the two-voice request idle.
Priority of the paired request, compared with the active priority before replacing it.
Pending effect number for SID voice two. $FF clears the request.
Voice-two sound request priority, checked against the current effect’s priority.
Holds the paired timer while set and permits the incoming request to retain the preceding effect as a follow-up.
Processes a queued request for SID voices one and three, ticks those voices, then processes and ticks the separate request for voice two.
If the effect duration reached zero, clears voices one and three and restores any saved request. Otherwise applies the current effect’s timing and modulation.
Decrements the duration unless the hold flag is set. Shifts through the configured effect bits, updating the two voices’ high frequency bytes as enabled.
One effect bit enables the offset sequence at $0599. Its $80 byte resets the sequence position, and each offset is added to the stored base frequency.
One effect bit adds a configured increment to the cutoff high byte and writes resonance and routing $F5.
The last two effect bits independently increment the high pulse-width bytes of voices one and three.
Reloads the effect flags for the next tick and writes both voices’ frequency high bytes.
A request with bit seven set returns immediately. Otherwise compares the request’s priority at $0401 with the active priority and drops requests that are lower.
Stores the accepted priority, multiplies the request number by sixteen and indexes the paired voice parameter table. Saves the old effect if the hold flag is set.
Remembers the accepted request, marks the queue empty and clears the voices before installing the effect’s control and envelope bytes.
Reads a sixteen-byte record for voices one and three. The first eight bytes set the control, envelope and pulse-width values. The remaining bytes set effect flags, pitch, duration and modulation.
Saved flags for the active paired effect, copied back after the current tick consumes a copy of the bits.
Shift register for the current tick’s paired-effect flags. Successive shifts test each enabled update.
Current voice-one frequency high byte for the paired effect, altered by the step or pitch sequence.
Current voice-three frequency high byte for the paired effect, changed by its own step.
Paired effect duration. The effect tick decrements it unless the hold byte is set.
Signed high-frequency step for voice one in the active paired effect.
High-frequency step added to the active pitch for voice three.
Priority retained for the active paired effect. Requests with a smaller priority are discarded.
Index into the paired-effect pitch sequence. $80 sends the next read back to sequence index zero.
Base value added to the selected pitch-sequence byte before updating voice one.
High pulse-width byte for voice one. The paired effect can increment it on a tick.
High pulse-width state for voice three, independently incremented and written to SID.
Eight-byte paired-effect pitch sequence, including its $80 loop marker.
Filter cutoff high byte accumulated while the paired effect is active.
Step added to the filter cutoff when the paired effect enables filter updates.
Effect number queued to follow the active paired effect, or $FF when no follow-up is pending.
Last paired request number, retained so the hold path can queue it again.

Transition status tested by the quest exit before following a world-load descriptor.
The loaded build returns immediately at this periodic hook and at the adjacent entry $0811.
Sets up the processor and stack, silences the SID, sets the initial life digit and clears the world transition bytes before calling the quest setup.
Resets the stack and display, then tests the world transition flag. Without a transition it decrements the life digit and branches to the restart when the digit stays nonnegative.
Copies the four bytes at $4F18 into the quest setup at $173A, clears control and effect state, marks the six entries at $BF40 with $FF, and enters the main quest path at $0A44.
State byte set during gameplay entry and tested by the quest transition control.
Calls the nested timing delay twice with the initial outer counter set to zero, then jumps to the gameplay setup at $0A44.
World transition selector used with the status byte at $07FF to index the disk-load descriptor table.
Request to leave the current quest loop. The transition code tests it before handling the next life or overlay.

Selects an eight-byte disk request record by testing the transition selector and the prior-load byte at $07FF. A negative selector chooses OPEN. A nonnegative selector after the first load chooses WIN for $0A and CL otherwise.
Disables interrupts and sprites, sets the low processor-port bits to $06 and restores the working zero page from $C802-$C8FF before making the disk request.
Sets logical file 1 on device 8, sets the filename from the copied record and pushes the return address before tail-jumping to the KERNAL LOAD entry.
The selected record starts with a continuation address minus one, followed by a byte retained from the descriptor, the filename length and four padded name bytes.
Two bytes pushed as the synthetic return for the next overlay LOAD call, copied from its descriptor.
Length field followed by the four-byte target filename for the pending overlay load.
Five eight-byte load descriptors in the order HL, IL, CL, WIN and OPEN. The two leading bytes are the synthetic return address for LOAD.
Initializes viewport, items and score display. Clears pending audio requests and installs the raster schedule before enabling the playfield.
Quest-loop phase counter. Its two low bits select the next group of work.
Runs one of four jobs using the low two bits of the loop counter: keyboard, character animation, score and health, or map actions. Then services sprite processing, timing and transition state.
Request for a full viewport rebuild. The main loop waits for its ready phase and clears this flag after the redraw.
If a redraw is pending and the viewport is at its ready phase, blanks the screen and rebuilds both viewport buffers and visible item state. Tests the world and life exit flags afterward.
Countdown used while the life-ending display keeps updating effects and animated characters.
Pending spell exchange flag, set by the item-contact path and cleared after opening the exchange.
Opens the pending spell exchange, then checks the deferred object request. Copies its saved coordinates and type into the constructor inputs and returns to the main loop.
Input-inhibit byte. Read by the joystick and keyboard service before accepting new input.
Secondary gameplay state byte set during setup and cleared when the playfield becomes active.
Display-update state set before a blanked redraw and cleared when the main loop resumes.
Sets the colour lookup from $4F2A and the two terrain lookup pointers to $5BB7 and $5C6B.
Initializes joystick, direction masks, subpixel offsets, jump and pose state. Sets the viewport direction countdown to seven.
Copies two world coordinates to the map origin and multiplies the matching player coordinates by eight for the pixel representation.

Saves banking, exposes I/O, runs the sound-effect service and restores the original processor port.
Calls the SID-effect driver at $0405 and returns to the display path.
Countdown for the sound-effect service after the quest start prompt is accepted.
Draws the localized start prompt and waits for Space or controller Fire while servicing controls and audio. After acceptance, waits on the raster and ticks the sound effects before returning.
Fills colour RAM, clears the central text area to glyph $A9 and copies 200 stored cell bytes from $0D15 to the bottom of the screen matrix.

Temporary message selection state consumed by the localized drawing path.

Saves the message number in $0DDE and draws the heading selected by language $C902. It then adds the language index to a message-group offset and draws that body through the same renderer.

Walks a screen text script through $11-$12. For each segment it calculates the two screen rows and their colour addresses. It converts glyph codes to pairs of character indices, writes $9A to both rows for a space, and interprets $FE as another segment and $FF as end.

Checks the selected spell slot and queues effect seven if it is empty. Otherwise waits for the viewport phase, saves the playfield state, sets the message screen and waits for input code five before restoring play.
Reads keys 1 through 4. Exchanges the selected spell for the offer in the corresponding slot, updates the inventory and sets the action bit associated with the received spell.
Looks up the previous spell’s packed action index and clears the corresponding bit in the action-state table.
Index of the spell surrendered in the exchange, reused when converting it to the action-state bit.
Index of the spell received in the exchange, reused when updating the corresponding action bit.
Fills slot $CA at $B280 with $AA. Sets four pairs of multicolour sprites on the same row. Each pair uses the selected spell icon and slot $CA, with pointers at $AFF8–$AFFF.

Uses bit four of $B0 to select the matrix at $C000 or $C400, translates its character codes through the colour table at ($BC), and fills colour RAM. Restores the HUD and playfield setup and re-enables raster interrupts.
Saved display mode restored after leaving the spell-exchange screen.
When the probe reports tile $79 and the request is empty, saves the probe’s map coordinates and queues replacement tile $7B.
Selects VIC bank $8000, points the matrix at $AC00 and glyphs at $B000, then sets the multicolour character display registers.
Installs $13D5 in RAM’s IRQ vector and the software BRK vector, selects the first raster line, masks both CIA sources and enables the VIC interrupt.
Saves A, X, Y and the port at $01, switches its low bits to $05 and acknowledges the VIC interrupt. For a raster interrupt it selects a stage address from $140E using twice the stage index at $42.
Little-endian targets for the two raster stages, $1416 and $147D.
High-byte base for the indirect raster-stage handler words. The dispatcher doubles its phase index.
Two raster compare values selected by the stage index, $F8 and $CB in the quest capture.
Low byte of the runtime indirect jump address used by the raster service.
High byte paired with the interrupt service pointer low byte at $1414.
Schedules the next raster IRQ and prepares the horizontal and vertical scroll phase from the current movement masks. Updates sprite hardware, processes the sound hook and advances the quest tick.

Waits until the raster passes $CD, briefly writes $7F to VIC control 1, clears the sprite X positions, switches the VIC to bank $8000 and selects the HUD bitmap and screen matrix there with $D018=$BF.
Temporary phase value used while selecting the next raster service.
Stage marker written around the per-frame gameplay jobs and restored by the IRQ exit.
Restores the old phase, clears the high raster compare, acknowledges and masks CIA 1, restores banking and registers and returns from interrupt.
Reads stacked status from $0107,X. A set break bit jumps to the RTI at $3B52.
Points the RAM NMI vector at $15FD. Stops both CIA 2 timers, masks their interrupt sources and acknowledges the pending state.
Loads the CIA 2 Timer B latch from $16A8–$16A9, starts its configured mode and enables its interrupt source.
Processor-port value saved when entering the secondary interrupt and restored immediately before RTI.
Selects VIC bank $C000 via CIA 2 and sets the screen mode and fine-scroll values from $B2 and $B4. Writes the screen and character memory selector from $B0.
Temporary value saved at the end of playfield raster register setup.
Programs the baseline world colours. Tests the viewport Y coordinate against the background boundary, then sets or schedules the secondary colour pair.
Low byte of the CIA Timer B latch for the background colour boundary.
High byte of the same timer latch calculated from the world boundary and movement phase.
Calculates the distance to the world’s colour boundary and adjusts the high timer byte for direction. Derives the low timer byte from the scroll phase table and starts the timer.
Eight low-timer phase values used when programming the timed background colour change.
Selects VIC bank $C000, sets background and sprite modes, loads two shared tile colours from the world header and selects the $F800 character set with $D018=$0F.
Low initial X coordinate, copied from the world header and later loaded into the player and map origin.
High initial X coordinate for the map origin and the player’s pixel-scaled start position.
Low initial Y coordinate restored at the start of a life or a queued redraw.
High initial Y coordinate loaded alongside the low byte as the viewport starting position.

Uses the world start coordinates at $173A-$173D to split the starting position into metatile indices and offsets within four-character tiles. Sets up the map pointer and patches the screen and colour RAM destination operands for the initial draw.
Fetches a metatile ID from the map through $9C, subtracts one to index the two offset tables and adds the world-specific character-grid base. A zero ID uses the separate fill path.

Reads individual character codes through $62, writes them through the patched screen destination, then looks up each colour through $BC. Advances through a four-character metatile segment and stops after 40 columns.
Low operand byte of the screen store at $185D, shared by the zero and nonzero character paths. The row update advances the address by 40.
High operand byte of the screen store at $185D, shared by the zero and nonzero character paths. The row update advances the address by 40.
Low operand byte of the colour RAM store after the character-colour lookup.
Upper operand byte of the patched colour store. The row update forms it by combining the screen page with the colour RAM bank bits.

Byte immediately before the pose frame delay lookup.

Checks flags that inhibit movement, then branches by base pose and vertical movement flag. Pose seven selects the crouch path. A pending turn uses $2418.
On flag $21E1, enters pose eight with frame zero or advances that animation until its final frame at $278C.
Horizontal motion advances the base walk cycle. Near the end of the cycle or when the stick is still, the state falls through to the standing and action checks.
Resets the base pose and frame. Tests Down before checking Fire, and starts the standing fire animation only when the existing shot timer is zero.
Advances pose three. At frame four and with no shot guard set, copies the configured timer into the shot timer and guard. Resets the pose at the last frame.

Enters display pose one and starts at frame zero. A later update advances the turn animation until its frame limit.
Selects base pose four or nine according to $21E5 and the counter at $259F. Resets the animation frame and directional mask when it changes the pose.
While the vertical movement flag is two, goes through the fall counter path. Otherwise advances the pose animation to its frame limit and resets the movement flags.
Advances $21E7 up to the limit held at $21E8. A type-zero active spell skips that increment. At 25 or more updates it suppresses horizontal input.
Copies the base pose and frame at $2798 and $279A into the display pose and frame bytes $2799 and $279B.
Clears the movement mask if $21E3 is set, then enters the common pose and sprite update.

Pending energy adjustment combined with the current value before redrawing the bar.

Four byte masks selected by the low two bits of the live energy value.

Flag produced for the selected active spell types and consulted by the display path.
Restores the world’s baseline colours. Checks the active spell and can request a world transition, set a pending health adjustment or update the two background colours.
Ticks selected active spell durations and checks the Return key when a spell is ready. Type 1 increments the life digit up to nine, while types 2 and 8 save and replace the weapon byte at $28F0.

Checks for an eligible selection with no active spell, then reads the Return key from CIA 1. Type 4 skips activation.
Sets the active flag and loads the selected type’s duration. Type 1 adds a life up to nine. Types 2 and 8 replace the weapon with values 3 and 4 and save the previous value.

Clears $2E17, then sets it for an active spell of type 0, 1, 3 or 6.
Checks Space through CIA 1. Releasing clears the repeat counter. Holding it repeatedly decrements the counter and reloads it with eight after it goes negative.

Clears the selected slot and the active flag, updates the HUD and advances the selection, wrapping after slot eight.
Scans up to nine slots from the selection, wrapping to zero if necessary. If every slot is empty, stores $FF as the available slot.
Enables sprite 0 on the HUD, sets its position and colour, and writes pointer $A7 plus the spell index at $AFF8.
Resets the spell-screen countdown, gets a new stream byte and uses three low bits to select a colour from $302D.

Part of the spell-colour area. The repeat service stores the newly selected colour here.
Colours selected with the low three bits of a fresh stream byte while processing the relevant spell effect.
Installs 160 screen matrix bytes at $AF20–$AFBF and 160 colour RAM entries at $DB20–$DBBF.
Screen matrix bitmap colour pairs copied to the HUD at $AF20–$AFBF.
The other cell colour selected from the colour RAM chip. This block copies to $DB20.

Two temporary coordinate words and the packed flag index used by the pickup handler.
